claim: New York and Colorado materials illustrate rising state-level consumer access and right-to-repair policy for electronics.

state_policy_sources.period: 2024 source page; effective date requires verification

repair_barrier_context.role: US repair-restriction and warranty mechanism context; not a phone outcome series

global_circularity_counter_signal.publisher: International Telecommunication Union / Global E-waste Monitor
global_circularity_counter_signal.boundary: Global aggregate e-waste and policy synthesis; not US phone repair volume, household replacement behavior, or causal policy evaluation.

why_not_pooled: State policy sources describe legal access and implementation, not realized repair behavior.
FTC evidence describes mechanisms and restrictions, not a representative phone-repair outcome panel.
ITU e-waste measures are global and aggregate, with different denominators and geography.
The three evidence lanes do not share a unit, population, period, or outcome definition that permits pooling.

target_outcome.name: US consumer electronics repair-access outcome panel
target_outcome.minimum_period: two comparable annual or quarterly periods before and after an explicitly dated policy change
target_outcome.population: US phone/device owners or repair transactions with a documented sampling or administrative frame

source_targets.artifact: complaints, enforcement, warranty, or repair-access records with dated denominators
source_targets.acceptance: phone/electronics scope and period are explicit; do not substitute general legal text for an outcome

source_targets.artifact: electronics collection/reuse/recycling series with device category and geography
source_targets.acceptance: repair/reuse is separable from recycling and denominator is documented

source_targets.publisher: independent repair transaction or consumer survey source
source_targets.artifact: dated repair volume, price, time-to-repair, replacement, or device-life panel
source_targets.acceptance: publisher, sampling frame, uncertainty, and rights are documented; vendor marketing alone is insufficient

acceptance_criteria: at least one dated outcome measure is independent of the state-policy source
the outcome has a compatible US device population and explicit denominator
policy exposure and implementation dates are verified from primary records
repair and recycling are not silently treated as the same outcome
counter-signals and non-exposed or comparison geographies are retained
stop_rule: Do not promote the IBIS claim, pool the state/FTC/ITU evidence, or run an internal company bridge if no comparable outcome frame, uncertainty, rights basis, and independent lineage can be obtained.
next_action: Acquire one dated US repair/replacement outcome series and reconcile its device population and denominator to the verified New York and Colorado policy effective dates.
boundary: This plan advances acquisition and comparison design; it is not evidence that right-to-repair policy increased repair volume or reduced e-waste.
